LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Conversational Skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Conversational Skills, part of Strand 7 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do you take turns in speaking during conversations? 2. Why is it important to interrupt appropriately in conversations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch recorded clips of conversations based on the theme,

2. role play using introductory and closing phrases in a conversation with peers,

3. work jointly to pick out appropriate expressions used as interjections to express emotion in oral conversations e.g. to s

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch recorded clips of conversations based on the theme,
2. role play using introductory and closing phrases in a conversation with peers,
3. work jointly to pick out appropriate expressions used as interjections to express emotion in oral conversations e.g. to s

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Conversational Skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner participates in a dialogue while using appropriate interjections and turn taking

skills.

• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by picking out appropriate expressions

used as interjections to express emotions in oral conversations.

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to organise and conduct a talent exhibition on various talents

and gifts during the school or class talents' day.

• Love: This is developed as the learner respects others when roleplaying a disagreement between characters using appropriate

turn taking skills and interrupting politely.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education and mentorship: This is promoted as the learner works to identify and grow their talents and gifts and that of

others.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate use of polite language in conversations to their learning of respect and care for others in

Religious Education.
